release_schedule.rule: The International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS), which adopts and periodically revises labour statistics resolutions such as this one, is 'hosted by the ILO every five years' (per ILOSTAT's ICLS standards page). The 19th ICLS (2013) originally adopted this resolution, the 20th ICLS was held 10-19 October 2018, and the 21st ICLS (October 2023) adopted a resolution amending this very resolution.
release_schedule.note: This is a standard-setting resolution, not a periodic statistical release. It is revisited only when the ICLS (convened roughly every five years by the ILO) chooses to review or amend it, as happened at the 21st ICLS in 2023. No 22nd ICLS date has been officially announced yet as of 2026-08-11; 2028 is a computed estimate based on the 5-year cadence (2013 -> 2018 -> 2023), not a confirmed date. There is no guarantee the 22nd ICLS agenda will include a revision of this specific resolution.

targetReport.title: Standard International Trade Classification (SITC)
targetReport.description: The United Nations' commodity classification for international merchandise trade, grouping traded goods by material, processing stage, market practice and end use so that trade can be analysed rather than merely tariffed. It is the analytical counterpart to the HS, which is the collection nomenclature: countries collect customs data on HS codes and convert to SITC for comparison and long-run series, which is exactly what the Chinese yearbooks wired here do. Held at family level deliberately — the documents in this corpus that cite it name no revision. Revisions: original 1950, Rev.1 (1961), Rev.2 (1975), Rev.3 (1986) and Rev.4, accepted by the UN Statistical Commission at its thirty-seventh session in March 2006 and recommended by the Interagency Task Force on International Merchandise Trade Statistics for analytical use.
targetReport.cadence_note: Five editions in fifty-six years and none since Rev.4 in 2006. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal so the pulse rate reads as near-static, matching the treatment of `isic` and `sna-2008`.

release_schedule.note: SITC has no publication calendar and no fixed revision cycle. Rev.4 (2006) is the current edition and UNSD's classification registry records its status as Operational as of a 2026-09-09 read; no successor has been announced. Unlike ISIC, SITC is not covered by the Committee of Experts' proposed five-year ISIC/CPC revision cycle, so no computable next revision date exists.

targetReport.title: System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008)
targetReport.publisher: United Nations, European Commission, IMF, OECD and World Bank
targetReport.description: The internationally agreed standard set of concepts, definitions, classifications and accounting rules for compiling national accounts, in force 2008-2025. Superseded by the 2025 SNA (UNSC 56th Session, March 2025) — see sna-2025. Retained here because the eight reports below still cite it by name as their methodology basis; country-level rollout of the successor targets 2029-2030, so nothing downstream is factually wrong yet.
targetReport.cadence_note: Revised roughly once a generation — previous editions 1953, 1968 and 1993. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal so the pulse rate reads as near-static.

release_schedule.note: Superseded by the 2025 SNA (UNSC 56th Session, March 2025) — see sna-2025's own published-calendar schedule for the adoption date and rollout window. No further revisions expected under the SNA 2008 edition.

targetReport.title: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, Sixth Edition (BPM6)
targetReport.description: The IMF's standard for compiling the balance of payments and the international investment position — the accounting framework for a country's transactions and positions with the rest of the world. Harmonised with SNA 2008. A seventh edition (BPM7) was developed alongside the 2025 SNA update. Country code is CA only because the schema offers no international option.
targetReport.cadence_note: Revised roughly once a generation — BPM5 in 1993, BPM6 in 2009. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal.

Projected next edition (successor to BPM7), based on the observed ~15-17 year revision cycle

release_schedule.note: BPM6 itself (the report this entry is about) is a one-off manual published in prepublication form Dec 2008 / final 2009 and is now superseded by BPM7, released 2025-03-20 (IMF press release PR25/072). The IMF revises this manual jointly with the UN's System of National Accounts (SNA) roughly every 15-17 years: BPM5 (1993) -> BPM6 (2008/2009, ~15-16 yrs) -> BPM7 (2025, ~16-17 yrs). No fixed/stated periodicity rule exists; the ~2041 date is a rough projection from the historical pattern, not an announced IMF target.

targetReport.title: Classification of the Purposes of Non-Profit Institutions Serving Households (COPNI)
targetReport.description: The United Nations classification of the outlays of non-profit institutions serving households by purpose. One of the four classifications of expenditure according to purpose published together as Statistical Papers Series M No. 84 (ST/ESA/STAT/SER.M/84), with COFOG, COICOP and COPP. UNSD's classification registry records it as operational, adopted 1999 and published 2000 (read 2026-10-24, HTTP 200). Minted 2026-10-24: Uzbekistan's national-accounts sheet names it beside COICOP and COFOG, which closed the `uz-national-accounts -> COPNI` lead.
targetReport.cadence_note: Not a periodic release. Adopted 1999, published 2000 in Series M No. 84; no later revision is recorded in the registry.
